Teacher Notes

December Music Bell-Ringers · 20 daily warm-ups · grades 3–6

How to use

  • Hand out one page as students arrive, or project it. Each page takes about 8 minutes; no prep, no pencil sharpening, no materials but a pencil.
  • A · Snowy Notes. Students write the letter name of every note in its box. Days 1–12 use one clef; from day 13 the page has a treble row and a bass row.
  • B · Mitten Rhythm. Write the count under each note and rest, at the place where it begins. A half note on beat 1 gets a 1; the 2 is held, so nothing is written for it. Write & for the half beat between beats. In 6/8 count 1 2 3 4 5 6.
  • C · Cocoa Symbols. Five symbols, five names in a word bank. Students write the letter. Two symbols are new each day until day 16, then the whole set rotates.
  • D · Skate Math. A measure is missing its ending. Students work out how many beats are missing.
  • Review aloud, or hand out the answer key. Answer keys are on pages 25–34, two days per page.
  • Print single-sided. Pages 3 and 4 are a student reference: note names, note values and a symbol glossary.

Great for

  • Band, orchestra, choir and general music, grades 3–6
  • The first five minutes of class, early finishers, sub plans and December weeks with a shorter schedule

Winter theme for every classroom

Snow, mittens, hot cocoa and ice skating. No holiday names or religious symbols, so the pages fit any school calendar.

The 20 days

DayThemeFocus
1SnowflakeTreble lines; quarter notes and rests
2MittensTreble spaces; half notes
3Hot CocoaTreble lines and spaces; half rests
4Ice SkatesLow treble notes; whole notes and rests
5Sled RunMiddle treble notes; 3/4 time
6Snow GlobeTreble clef C4 to A5; 2/4 and 3/4 time
7Warm ScarfTreble clef, all notes; eighth notes
8IciclesTreble clef, all notes; eighth notes in 3/4
9SnowballBass lines; eighth rests
10Warm BootsBass spaces; dotted half notes in 3/4
11Pine TreesBass lines and spaces; dotted half notes in 4/4
12Snow DayBass clef, all notes; rhythm review
13FiresideTreble and bass together; dotted quarter and eighth
14Winter StarsTreble and bass; dotted quarter and eighth in 2/4
15Skating PondTreble and bass; rhythm review
16Snow FortTreble and bass; first steps in 6/8
17EarmuffsTreble and bass; 6/8 with quarters and eighths
18Snowy OwlTreble and bass; 4/4 and 6/8 mixed
19Icy WindowTreble and bass; every meter
20Winter BreakChallenge: the whole set

Standards

Practices reading and identifying notation: pitch names, rhythm and meter, and music symbols. Supports the National Core Arts Standards for Music (MU:Pr4.2, grades 3–6). Modest claim: one short daily practice, not a full curriculum.

Every page is generated and checked: notes are placed by staff position, every measure adds up to its time signature, and each key is built from the same data as its page. No songs, lyrics or copyrighted characters are used.

Student Reference: Notes

Keep this page nearby while you work.

Treble clef · C4 (middle C) to A5

Lines (bottom to top): E G B D F — Every Good Boy Does Fine · Spaces: F A C E — FACE. Letters in blue are the notes in the spaces.

Bass clef · E2 to C4 (middle C)

Lines (bottom to top): G B D F A — Good Boys Do Fine Always · Spaces: A C E G — All Cows Eat Grass.

Note and rest values · in 4/4, 3/4 and 2/4

whole note4 beats
half note2 beats
quarter note1 beat
eighth note½ beat
dotted half note3 beats
dotted quarter note1½ beats
whole rest4 beats of silence
half rest2 beats of silence
quarter rest1 beat of silence
eighth rest½ beat of silence

A dot adds half the note's value: a half note is 2 beats, a dotted half note is 3 beats. In 6/8 the eighth note gets one count: a quarter note is 2 counts, a dotted quarter is 3.

Counting: 4/4 → 1 2 3 4 · 3/4 → 1 2 3 · 2/4 → 1 2 · eighth notes add & between beats (1 & 2 &) · 6/8 → 1 2 3 4 5 6.

Student Reference: Symbols

21 symbols you will meet in the Cocoa Symbols warm-ups.
treble clefMarks the G line. Used for higher notes.
bass clefMarks the F line. Used for lower notes.
quarter rest1 beat of silence.
sharpRaises a note by a half step.
flatLowers a note by a half step.
fortePlay loudly.
pianoPlay softly.
half rest2 beats of silence. It sits on the line.
time signatureTop: beats in a measure. Bottom: the note that gets one beat.
fermataHold the note longer than written.
naturalCancels a sharp or a flat.
whole restA whole measure of silence. It hangs from the line.
repeat signGo back and play the section again.
crescendoGradually get louder.
decrescendoGradually get softer.
mezzo fortePlay medium loud.
staccatoPlay short and separated.
accentPlay the note with extra emphasis.
final barlineMarks the end of the piece.
double barlineMarks the end of a section.
tieJoins two notes of the same pitch into one longer note.
